page: Amazon Web Services r8id.32xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 64-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor delivering 128 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache and advanced vector capabilities including AVX-512 and AMX matrix instructions. The instance is configured with 1024 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8 GB of RAM per core. Integrated hardware includes 7600 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, with zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional throughput in multi-threaded computation, data manipulation, and memory-bound tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress testing, Geekbench multi-core compute, and Clang software compilation. In database-centric evaluations, it recorded over 208 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database scores. Memory subsystem tests show high cached read bandwidth alongside strong uncached streaming rates, while hardware matrix extensions deliver fast prompt evaluation speeds across multiple large language model sizes.

The dense hardware allocation delivers strong architectural efficiency for data pipelines that require low-latency I/O, as the bundled 7600 GB local NVMe SSD array minimizes reliance on external network-attached storage. Single-threaded metrics fall closer to the median tier, indicating that workloads must leverage concurrent threads to fully exploit the underlying compute capacity. The server is well positioned for enterprise in-memory databases, distributed memory caches, real-time streaming analytics, and heavy ETL processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8id.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by a 64-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 128 vCPUs operating at up to 3.9 GHz and backed by 480 MB of L3 cache. It provides 1024 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory alongside 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded processing, reflected in high scores across PassMark database operations, Clang compilation, and Redis throughput exceeding 208 million operations per second. Hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions accelerates prompt processing in large language models. The combination of large memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage offers strong efficiency for I/O-intensive architectures without relying solely on remote volumes. This instance is suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data warehousing, and high-concurrency batch processing.
